  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The plan gives different repo counts for the @stable sync and the blocked-issue sweep without explaining whether the sweep includes coding-workflows.
  WHY: The sweep budget and `--repos-file` argument must match the actual repo count; otherwise the sweep may make an unnecessary call or miss issues in coding-workflows.
- docs/plans/retire-master-session-plan.md:129-130, 213 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]

  WHY: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` has at least two additional `Status: BLOCKED` stops at lines 68 and 92; rewiring only the 10 listed stop ids leaves those stops waiting for a human, contrary to goal G1.
- docs/plans/retire-master-session-plan.md:240-242 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The plan omits adding `secrets.GH_PAT` to the watchdog workflow environment despite requiring cross-repo reads and comments.
  WHY: `.github/workflows/claude-issue-queue-watchdog.yml:37-46` currently only has `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`, which is scoped to coding-workflows, so consumer-repo reads and comments will fail.
- docs/plans/retire-master-session-plan.md:236-237 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The plan adds pickup scanning and actions for blocked issues without updating the pickup Rules section that forbids reading target issues or acting on them.
  WHY: `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md:73` says the pickup never reads target issues, while the planned step 3c scans blocked issues and applies actions, leaving the command self-contradictory.

- docs/plans/retire-master-session-plan.md:§14 constraint vs Phase 2 approach and budget
  severity: NIT
  confidence: 3
  PROBLEM: The plan states two different repo counts: 13 for the @stable sync reach, but 14 for the sweep. The plan does not explain whether the sweep covers coding-workflows itself in addition to the 13 consumer repos, or whether one of the counts is wrong.
  WHY: The sweep's API budget (14 list calls) and the implementation's `--repos-file` argument (14 vs 13) must match the actual registered repo count. A mismatch would either over-call (one call returns 404) or under-call (missing blocked issues in coding-workflows itself, the very repo that runs the sweep). The plan should either state that the sweep covers 14 repos (13 consumers + coding-workflows) or align both counts.
